Zen is deliberately not on Google Play or the App Store. A store can remove the app at any moment or demand changes — and Zen is meant to be independent, including from big companies and from politics. Zen ma zmienić nie tylko media społeczno: Zen is meant to change not just social media, but also how people make decisions together. The “Pyramid” is built from cells of a few people who know each other personally; votes, delegated trust and a shared treasury flow from the bottom up, anonymous to everyone else, with no headquarters that could be bought off or shut down. It’s an attempt at a democracy that truly belongs to the people.
Zen nie ma konta w chmurze. Twój telefon: Zen has no cloud account. Your phone connects directly to your friends’ phones over a mesh network. Messages are end-to-end encrypted, and everything on the device is encrypted with your password. Nobody — not the author, not any company — can read your conversations. Losing your phone isn’t enough for someone to get to your data without your password.
Zen nie ma własnych serwerów. Telefony i: Zen has no servers of its own. Phones and computers connect through Yggdrasil — an open, encrypted network where every device has its own address, and traffic goes directly or through other devices that can't see the content. Direct messages are end-to-end encrypted by the Yggdrasil network itself. Zen adds its own encryption where content sits outside that connection: in copies held by friends (the mailbox), in entries for chosen recipients, in dating and similar places.
Zen nie odbiera w tle: Zen isn’t receiving in the background
Zen to komunikator i sieć dla ludzi, któ:
Zen is a messenger and network for people who know each other — but with no company in the middle. There’s no server that sees everything, no ads and no algorithm deciding what you see. Messages, photos and posts go directly between your friends’ phones and computers, encrypted, and your data stays on your device.

Beyond chats and calls, Zen helps you actually meet up: a “right now” status, events and dinners through friends, neighbors from your building, dating through mutual friends, help from those closest to you, and an alarm. And the “Pyramid” lets people organize and decide for themselves — from the bottom up, with no parties or institutions above.
